title: A priority-based thread pool
context: How would you design a thread pool that runs higher-priority tasks first?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Java concurrency questions (3 of 3)
source.note: Translated and condensed into English; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: Use a PriorityBlockingQueue as the work queue. Wrap each task in a class that implements Comparable or Comparator with a priority field. Submit that wrapper through execute, so the pool's queue orders tasks by priority. Because the queue is unbounded, add a capacity check yourself. Watch out for starvation of low-priority tasks, and consider aging. Note that submit wraps tasks in a FutureTask, which is not Comparable, so use execute or override newTaskFor to return a comparable task.

points.title: Priority queue
points.why: PriorityBlockingQueue hands the highest-priority task to the next free worker.

points.title: Starvation
points.why: Low-priority tasks can wait forever under constant high-priority load, so add aging.
